newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Pakistan's PIA seeks 225,000/T 1997/98 jet fuel.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan's PIA seeks 225,000/T 1997/98 jet fuel.

text.p: Pakistan International Airlines (PIA) has issued a term tender to buy 225,000 tonnes of aviation jet fuel for August 1997-June 1998 deliveries, a PIA source said on Monday.
The tender closes on July 16, he said.
The volume it seeks in this tender is unchanged from what it took for fiscal 1996-1997 (July 1-June 30).
PIA had earlier indicated that it would need 250,000 tonnes of jet fuel for its new fiscal year to meet increased flight routes and frequencies.
"The lower than expected volume is due to the shorter laycan for this tender," the source said.
PIA has been buying term jet fuel from state-owned Kuwait Petroleum Corp (KPC) since 1993 after Kuwait recovered from the 1990/1991 Gulf War.
The 1996/1997 contract was awarded at a premium of $1.45 per barrel to MidEast spot quotes, on a cost-insurance-freight (cif) basis to Karachi.
In 1995/1996, PIA bought 175,000 tonnes from KPC at a $1.20-premium to MidEast spot quotes, cif Karachi.
